Baseline: The statement’s acknowledgment of strong Q3 growth and elevated inflation is modestly hawkish and consistent with holding rates at 5.25–5.50% with ongoing QT. However, SLOOS points to a clear tightening in credit supply across categories that tempers this hawkishness. Banks reported tighter standards and wider spreads for C&I and CRE loans (especially at large and foreign banks), citing higher funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, and declines in the market value of fixed‑income assets; foreign banks also cited collateral values and ease of selling loans. Consumer credit (credit cards, autos) is also tighter with lower approval likelihood and greater sensitivity to FICO scores, while residential real estate and HELOCs show tighter terms and softer demand. These SLOOS findings reinforce that “tighter financial and credit conditions” are likely to weigh on activity and inflation, supporting a cautious, hold‑biased stance rather than additional near‑term firming. Netting strong growth/elevated inflation against broad-based credit tightening shifts the tone from mildly hawkish to near‑neutral/slightly cautious.
